//: Hand-edited corrections applied to the Bedrock-sourced entity_models.json / entity_geometry.json. Loaded by EntityModelLoader per entity; keys are `geometry_ref`, `texture_ref`, `inventory_y_rotation`, `bone_overrides`, `hidden_bones`. `hidden_bones` strips bones Bedrock packs into the shared geometry but Java conditionally hides at render time (saddlebags on plain horses, saddles on undead mounts).

entities.//minecraft:armor_stand: ArmorStandModel constructor statically sets this.hat.visible = false; vanilla bounds-walker honours visibility and excludes the hat extent. Our pipeline doesn't track per-bone visibility, so strip the hat at load time. Same applies to any model whose constructor statically toggles visibility before render. Detect at tooling time when convenient and remove this hand-edited entry.
entities.//illager-family: IllagerModel constructor sets this.hat.visible = false. Pillager / vindicator / evoker keep that default; their renderers don't re-enable the hat. IllusionerRenderer explicitly sets this.model.getHat().visible = true so illusioner DOES render with a hat - it must NOT be on this hidden_bones list. The vindicator / evoker entries below also list 'rightArm' / 'leftArm' for bedrock-pipeline cleanup; those are unrelated to the Java-pipeline hat-visibility issue.
entities.//minecraft:skeleton_horse: Bedrock authors the skeleton horse leg cubes with the bone silhouette texture pushed onto faces that don't face the camera in our standard iso pose. Front-right Leg3 (X=+4, Z=-8) needs -90 yaw and front-left Leg4 (X=-4, Z=-8) needs +90 yaw to swing their bone-face into the iso-visible set; rear legs Leg1/Leg2 (Z=11) both need 180 yaw. Each leg bone has a single cube and no parent, so bone-level rotation with no explicit pivot rotates the cube about its own bbox center (the default introduced 2026-04-26).
entities.//minecraft:cow_cold: ColdCowModel registers a separate LayerDefinition (ModelLayers.COLD_COW) with a 3-cube body (base + inflated 0.5 fur + udder strip) and a head whose horns are child bones with PartPose.offsetAndRotation(±, -2.5, -3.5 or -5, PI/2, 0, 0). Bytecode tooling only scans top-level renderer registrations; variant ModelLayers aren't surfaced. Hand-edit redirects minecraft:cow_cold at geometry.cold_cow.
entities.//minecraft:cow_warm: WarmCowModel REPLACES head with an inline 6-cube list (base head + muzzle + 4 horn cubes including 2 mirrored at +X positions). Same tooling miss as cow_cold; hand-edit redirects at geometry.warm_cow.
entities.//minecraft:chicken_cold: ColdChickenModel REPLACES body (base + 0x3x5 plane-cube tail at uv (38, 9)) and head (base + 6x3x4 crown at uv (44, 0)). Replacing head wipes beak + red_thing children since addOrReplaceChild's new CubeListBuilder doesn't re-register them. Variant ModelLayers.COLD_CHICKEN not surfaced by tooling; hand-edit redirects at geometry.cold_chicken. The warm chicken variant (chicken_variant/warm.json) has no model override and falls through to AdultChickenModel - it's a family-fit canvas issue, not a geometry issue, so chicken_warm stays on geometry.adultchicken.
entities.//minecraft:pig_cold: ColdPigModel REPLACES body with base 10x16x8 + inflated 0.5 fur layer (uv (28, 32)). Head and legs inherited. Variant ModelLayers.COLD_PIG not surfaced by tooling; hand-edit redirects at geometry.cold_pig. The warm pig variant (pig_variant/warm.json) has no model override and falls through to PigModel - same family-fit canvas issue as chicken_warm.
entities.//minecraft:rabbit: RabbitRenderer.getTextureLocation reads state.variant via state.isToast check then RABBIT_LOCATIONS map. Vanilla's zero-state Rabbit constructor defaults variant to BROWN (the first Rabbit.Variant enum value); our tooling-extracted texture_ref defaulted to rabbit_toast. Sampling the vanilla render's body pixels confirms dark brown (97, 72, 52) - matches rabbit_brown.
entities.//minecraft:axolotl: AxolotlRenderer.getTextureLocation looks up state.variant in TEXTURE_BY_TYPE. Vanilla's zero-state default is LUCY (pink/white); the central body pixel of the vanilla render is (227, 132, 188) which matches axolotl_lucy's signature pink. Ours was set to axolotl_blue.
entities.//minecraft:stray: Vanilla StrayRenderer adds a SkeletonClothingLayer (ModelLayers.STRAY_OUTER_LAYER + stray_overlay.png). STRAY_OUTER_LAYER is HumanoidModel.createMesh(CubeDeformation(0.25F), 0.0F) - the standard skeleton mesh with every cube inflated by 0.25 pixels. Without this overlay the skeleton-only silhouette is missing the frost-cloak content that protrudes laterally.
entities.//minecraft:bogged: Vanilla BoggedRenderer adds a SkeletonClothingLayer (ModelLayers.BOGGED_OUTER_LAYER + bogged_overlay.png). BOGGED_OUTER_LAYER is HumanoidModel.createMesh(CubeDeformation(0.2F), 0.0F) - skeleton mesh with inflate 0.2. Bogged's base geometry already includes the mushroom bones; this overlay supplies the inflated humanoid silhouette that vanilla renders on top.
entities.//minecraft:magma_cube: Bedrock authors slime/magmacube_v2.png with low partial alpha throughout, expecting their additive renderer to glow the cube. Java has no separate emissive PNG (MagmaCubeRenderer uses entityCutoutNoCull). Without an opaque world background to additively brighten over, the static iso renderer needs the texture bumped to opaque so the magma colors render at full saturation. force_opaque applies the bump at load time without mutating the bundled PNG.
entities.//minecraft:spider: Bedrock bakes the eye glow into spider/spider.png as alpha=3 spots. With the Part 1 emissive overlay supplying the bright eye glow, the body's alpha=3 spots would render as faint translucent ghosts against the transparent canvas - force_opaque promotes them back to opaque so the body face is solid behind the emissive glow.
entities.//minecraft:cave_spider: Same partial-alpha eye-spot pattern as spider; same force_opaque rationale.
entities.//minecraft:cat: Vanilla Java's AdultFelineModel.setupAnim sets `tail2.xRot = 1.7278761f + amplitude * cos(walkPos) * walkSpeed` on three sibling state branches (sprinting/walking/crouching). The static rest pose (walkSpeed=0) collapses to 1.7278761 rad = ~99 deg - the bend at the tail1/tail2 joint that gives a cat its hooked-tail silhouette. tail1's rotation lives in createBodyLayer and is auto-captured by the bind-pose scraper; tail2's lives only inside setupAnim so the scraper misses it. We override BOTH bones with bone-level rotation (not bind-pose) so the chain propagates from tail1 to tail2 - bind-pose only rotates the bone's own cubes, leaving children at their authored joint, which would detach tail2 from tail1's swept-up tip. The override on tail1 also clears the auto-generated bind_pose_rotation (see applyBoneOverrides) to avoid stacking the same 51.566 deg twice. tail1 pivot [0, 9, 8] and tail2 pivot [0, 9, 16] are the geometry's authored joints so each segment swings from its base. Texture: vanilla's zero-state cat variant resolves to the BLACK (tuxedo) entry from data/minecraft/cat_variant/black.json - all variants except all_black (which is structure-gated to witch huts via cats_spawn_as_black) are priority=0 unconditional, and the harness picks alphabetically first: black. The tuxedo pattern has a black body + white chest / paws + gray collar, dominant rgb (28, 24, 39) and (234, 234, 234). Our tooling default cat_all_black is the uniform-black stray variant; cat_black is the tamed-tuxedo variant the harness renders.
entities.//minecraft:ocelot: Same AdultFelineModel.setupAnim tail2 constant as cat - the geometries (geometry.cat / geometry.ocelot.v1.8) share the tail bone pivots and the Java model class.
entities.//minecraft:blaze: Bedrock geometry.blaze authors 12 upperBodyParts0..11 bones all stacked at the same pivot (0, 24, 0) with identical cube origins (0, 16, 0); Java BlazeModel.createBodyLayer distributes them via PartPose.offset across three rings of four rods each. Outer ring (parts 0..3) at radius 9 sits above the head pivot (Java jy=-2+cos(i*0.5)); middle ring (parts 4..7) at radius 7 just below (jy=2+cos(i*0.5), angles offset by pi/4); inner ring (parts 8..11) at radius 5 well below the head (jy=11+cos(i*0.75), angles offset by 3*pi/20). Java Y points down in model space so Bedrock dy = -jy. The bind-pose scraper only captures rotations from PartPose.offsetAndRotation, not pure translations, so the offsets don't reach entity_bind_poses.json. We materialise the 12 rod positions here as extra_bones templated from upperBodyParts0, then hide the 12 stacked originals. force_opaque bumps the alpha=90 baked rod texture to opaque at load time - additive over the transparent canvas would dim the rods to ~35% saturation.
entities.//minecraft:sheep: Vanilla Java composes a normal sheep from two layers - SheepModel renders the actual sheep body (full long legs, snouted head, tan skin) and SheepFurModel overlays the white wool covering on top (wool body + short leg-stubs + small head, no snout). Bedrock ships these as separate geometries: geometry.sheep.sheared.v1.8 is the skin and geometry.sheep.v1.8 is the wool. With only the wool geometry assigned to minecraft:sheep, the actual sheep body underneath is invisible. Re-root the entity at the sheared geometry so the skin is the base layer, then overlay the wool. Both share the sheep/sheep texture which packs the skin UVs in the top half and the wool UVs in the bottom half. force_opaque bumps the ~600 wool-fluff partial-alpha texels to opaque at load time so the body and legs render solid instead of as a translucent speckled outline.
entities.//minecraft:sheep_sheared: Bedrock's standalone sheared sheep geometry uses the same sheep/sheep texture as the woolly sheep above. The wool-fluff partial-alpha texels would render the body+legs as a translucent speckle without force_opaque.
entities.//minecraft:slime: Vanilla Java SlimeModel renders two stacked cubes: a 6x6x6 inner body and an 8x8x8 outer shell drawn translucent (entity/slime/slime.png with alpha=180 in the outer-shell UV strip at [0, 0]). Bedrock's geometry.slime only ships the inner cube + eyes/mouth - the outer shell isn't a separate Bedrock bone, just a UV strip on the same texture that vanilla Java composes via SlimeOuterLayer. Synthesize the outer cube as an extra bone templated from the inner cube. The outer-shell strip on slime.png is authored at 8-pixel face dimensions (TOP+BOTTOM occupy u 8..24 v 0..8, sides occupy u 0..32 v 8..16), so the override sets size=[8, 8, 8] and origin_offset=[-1, -1, -1] explicitly rather than templating from the inner's 6x6x6 with inflate - the strip-unwrap formula keys off size, not size+inflate, and a 6-sized strip would sample empty pixels. Texture's authored alpha=180 in that region renders as proper translucency without any per-overlay alpha flag.
entities.//minecraft:armadillo: Bedrock geometry.armadillo ships both 'body' (standing pose) and 'body_rolled_up' (defensive ball pose) bones; Java's ArmadilloModel toggles visibility per entity state at runtime. Without animation state we default to the standing pose; hide the rolled-up bone.
entities.//minecraft:guardian: Bedrock geometry.guardian.v1.8 stacks all 12 'spikepart0..11' bones at the same pivot (0, 24, 0) with identical cubes; Java's GuardianModel distributes them at runtime to the 12 edge midpoints of the body cube (16x16x16 spanning Bedrock X/Z [-8, +8] and Y [0, 16]) via SPIKE_X/SPIKE_Y/SPIKE_Z arrays plus per-spike rotations from SPIKE_X_ROT/Y_ROT/Z_ROT (each multiplied by pi). Y axis is flipped between Java (Y-down) and Bedrock (Y-up), so Bedrock cube_offset Y = -16 - SPIKE_Y[i] (which lands the spike pivot at body Y = 8 - SPIKE_Y[i], with the body Y midpoint at 8). Pitch axis is also flipped so Bedrock pitch = -SPIKE_X_ROT*180; same flip on yaw and roll. Eye cube was authored at z=0 (inside body); Java's createBodyLayer offsets it z=-8.25 so it sits on the body's front face - mirror that with cube_offset.
entities.//minecraft:elder_guardian: Bedrock pipeline: same geometry as guardian (geometry.guardian.v1.8) so reuse all the spike/eye overrides. Vanilla Java has a separate guardian_elder.png texture (paler, larger-looking variant) that the Bedrock pack doesn't ship; bundled from the Java client jar via FORCED_EXTRA_TEXTURE_REFS. The bedrock-style texture_ref 'guardian_elder' resolves against the flat bedrock cache. Java pipeline: redirect at geometry.guardian_elder (in entity_geometry_java_handedits.json), which carries the MeshTransformer.scaling(2.35F) applied to ALL 17 bones - the bytecode tooling missed scaling the 12 loop-added spike bones in geometry.guardian_1, so spikes were rendered tiny and detached from the scaled body. The java pipeline's texture_ref precedence requires a slash, so bedrock-style 'guardian_elder' here is skipped for Java and Java's entity-row 'guardian/guardian_elder' takes over.
entities.//minecraft:vindicator: Bedrock geometry.vindicator.v1.8 ships both arm sets - 'arms' folded across the chest (idle pose) plus 'rightArm'/'leftArm' hanging straight down (aggressive pose). Java's IllagerModel toggles visibility per entity state at runtime. Without animation state we default to the folded idle pose; hide the hanging pair so only crossed arms render. Also hide the hat (java-pipeline IllagerModel constructor sets hat.visible=false).
entities.//minecraft:evoker: Same illager rig as vindicator - both arm sets ship together. Hide the hanging pair so only the folded idle pose renders. Also hide the hat (java-pipeline IllagerModel constructor sets hat.visible=false).
entities.//minecraft:copper_golem_flower: Bedrock authors geometry.copper_golem.flower as a thin overlay carrying just the right_arm holding the flower (no body, head, or legs); vanilla Java composes the full golem by rendering the base mesh first and the flower mesh on top. Re-root the entity's base at geometry.copper_golem so the auto-fit anchors on the full body silhouette (matching the plain copper_golem icon size), then layer the flower-only geometry on top with its own texture. Same coordinate frame on both geometries means no per-overlay placement is needed.
entities.//minecraft:creeper_charged: Vanilla Java draws the standard creeper mesh and texture, then a translucent inflated 'power' overlay using entity/creeper/creeper_armor.png - that lightning-grid texture is what makes a charged creeper visually distinct from a plain creeper. Bedrock packs the inflated geometry as geometry.creeper.charged.v1.8 so the variant ships with the right mesh; this override re-roots the entity's base layer at the plain creeper geometry/texture and adds the charged geometry with the creeper_armor texture as an overlay. The creeper_armor.png ref must be present in entity_textures/creeper/ - if it's missing (the texture isn't bundled by ToolingEntityModels until the user runs ./gradlew entityModels with the forced-extra-texture list) the overlay drops silently and the renderer degrades to a plain creeper.
entities.//minecraft:snow_golem: Bedrock arm1/arm2 share identical cube geometry (origin [1,20,-1] size [12,2,2]) and rely on the animation system to rotate arm2 around yaw 180 for the opposite stick. With no animations here both arms stack in +X. Java SnowGolemModel's bind pose rotates the arms around Z by ~57.3 degrees; we mirror that here. arm2 also takes yaw 180 so it extends in -X instead of +X. Explicit pivot is the arm's bone pivot at the body shoulder so the rotations articulate at the joint (the default cube-center anchor would not flip arm2 to the body's other side and would not roll arm1 outward from the shoulder).
entities.//minecraft:fox: Bedrock fox body is authored vertically and laid horizontal via a Java-side 90 deg pitch bind pose. bindPoseRotation in this renderer only affects the bone's own cubes - tail (child of body) stays vertical and looks 90 deg off. Override tail with its own 90 deg pitch to follow the body. Explicit pivot is the tail's bone pivot at the body-tail joint (the default cube-center anchor would rotate the tail about its midpoint instead of swinging from its base).
entities.//minecraft:wolf: Bedrock authors upperBody (the mane/scruff) at pivot (-1, 10, 2) with cube Z=[-1, 6] - the back of the body. Java's upper_body bind pose anchors at pivot (-1, 14, -3) - 5 units forward, at the neck/head junction. applyBindPoses sets only the rotation, not the pivot, so our 90 deg pitch rotates around Bedrock's back-pivot and leaves the mane visually too far back. Shift the cube +5 forward in Z so the resulting pivot lands at Z=-3 (matching Java's anchor) and the bind-pose rotation hinges from the correct point.
entities.//minecraft:enderman: Bedrock geometry.enderman.v1.8 authors the head cube at Y=[24,32], overlapping the bottom of the body (Y=[26,38]) - the head sits inside the chest. The hat (child of head) is correctly positioned at Y=[38,45], at the top of the body where the head should be. Java's EndermanModel places the head pivot at the top of the body (Y=38). Shift the head cube +14 in Y so it lands above the body (Y=[38,46]) and aligns with the already-correct hat.
entities.//minecraft:chicken: No override needed: Bedrock authors leg0/leg1 (3x5x3 cubes at uv 26, 0) with the leg silhouette on the SOUTH face (col 36, rows 3-7) and the foot bottom on the DOWN face (cols 32-34, rows 0-2). Both are back-facing in our standard iso pose [pitch=30, yaw=225]. EntityGeometryKit.shouldCullBackFaces auto-detects this case: cubes whose iso-visible faces (TOP/NORTH/EAST) have empty UV rects but whose iso-hidden faces (DOWN/SOUTH/WEST) have content opt out of back-face culling, so the back faces render at their natural cube positions - foot at the cube's bottom, silhouette on the back face. Same applies to chicken_cold (same geometry layout).
entities.//minecraft:ender_dragon: Bedrock dragon.geo authors duplicated right-side parts (wing1, wingtip1, rearlegtip1, rearfoot1, frontlegtip1, frontfoot1) with cube origins identical to their left siblings, relying on Molang animations to translate the mirror into place. Tips and feet are also authored X-centred (origin X symmetric about 0) relying on Molang to slot them under each parent leg. We fill the gap with cube_offset shifts that land each duplicate under the correct leg column and mirror wingtip1 to the +X side.

minecraft:ender_dragon.//head_neck_y_shift: Bedrock authoring places head/neck bone cubes at Y=[16,32]/[19,29] centered at Y=24, well above the body's Y=[-4,20] center 8. Java's authoritative layout has head in FRONT of the body at similar Y, not above it. Corrective shift Y=-16 brings head/neck cubes down to the body's Y range so the head/neck plug into the body front rather than perching on top.
minecraft:ender_dragon.//legs_note: Java EnderDragonModel applies pitch rotations in a legâ†’tipâ†’foot hierarchy: frontleg 1.3 rad (74.48 deg), frontlegtip -0.5 rad (-28.65) relative, frontfoot 0.75 rad (42.97) relative. Rear: leg 1.0 rad (57.30), tip 0.5 rad (28.65), foot 0.75 rad (42.97). Bedrock authors tips/feet as root-level bones with cubes at X=0, relying on the animation system to chain them. We reparent each tip to its leg and each foot to its tip so the rotation chain propagates, then shift cubes so each part attaches at the end of its parent. Each rotation uses an explicit `pivot` at the bone's authored joint anchor - without it, the new default would rotate about each cube's own center and break joint articulation. Rotations use Bedrock sign convention (+pitch = forward tilt = top-of-bone moves toward -Z).
minecraft:ender_dragon.//extra_bones: Dragon tail: Java EnderDragonModel builds 12 tail segments at PartPose.offset(0, 10, 60 + i*10) as copies of the shared neck cube. Templated from the (post-override) neck which is already Y-shifted down by -16, so the tail inherits the corrected Y position without a separate Y shift here.

entities.//minecraft:breeze: Bedrock geometry.breeze authors three 2x8x2 rod cubes for the 'wind funnel' that vanilla animates around the central Y axis. We render a static inverted-pyramid tripod: rod tops anchored near the body silhouette edge, bottoms tilted inward toward a near-converging apex below the body center. Pivots: cube[0] (front) at (0, 21, -5), cube[1]/cube[2] (rear) at (+/-5.196, 21, 4) - radii ~5-6 in their respective directions, all raised 2 units in Y from the authored geometry so rod tops sit at body bottom (Y=21). Rotations target each rod's bottom at 35deg inward tilt while preserving cube orientation consistency: cube[0] uses pure pitch [35, 0, 0]; cube[1]/cube[2] use compound Euler angles [131, +/-40.5, -/+143.2] solved so the rotated cube's NORTH face matches cube[0]'s NORTH after a Y-rotation - keeps the texture wrap visually consistent across all three rods (without this 'twist' constraint the side rods looked rotated wrong on their long axis). Origin offsets shift each cube to keep the authored +2 Z pivot-to-cube-top offset.
